Farm Security Administration — US 1935-1944 documentary programme.

walkthroughs.body_html: The Farm Security Administration (1935-1944) commissioned Lange, Walker Evans, Gordon Parks and others to document Depression America. Lange's Migrant Mother (1936) became its emblematic image.
Robert Capa waded ashore at Omaha Beach on 6 June 1944. Of 106 frames shot, eleven survived a lab accident — the 'Magnificent Eleven' that defined war photography for a generation.
In 1947, Capa, Cartier-Bresson, Rodger and Seymour founded Magnum Photos — a photographer-owned cooperative ensuring photographers retained authorial control of their negatives.

numericals.q: Capa shot 106 D-Day frames but only how many survived (the 'Magnificent Eleven')?
